title: Agree structure
and content
steps.description: We map the pages, agree what each one has to do, and work out what content exists and what has to be written. Nothing gets designed against a page whose job is still undecided.

title: Design it, or
take your design
steps.description: We design the site against that structure, or we take the Figma file you supply and tell you upfront where something is expensive to build in Framer.

title: Build in Framer,
CMS wired
steps.description: We build the pages as reusable components and wire the collections behind them, so a new post or case study is a CMS entry rather than a new page.

title: Launch, train,
hand over
steps.description: We publish, point the domain, check the redirects, and sit with your team while they add a page themselves. You leave owning the site.

items.question: Can our team edit it after launch?
items.answer: That is the point of building it this way. Pages are made of components and the content sits in CMS collections, so adding a post or a case study is filling in fields, not editing a layout. We train your team on the site itself before handover. If you would rather not touch it, we keep a retainer for edits and new pages — but it is an option, not a condition of the build.

items.question: Do we need to supply designs?
items.answer: Either way works. We can design the site ourselves against the structure we agree, or build from a Figma file you supply. If you bring the designs, we will tell you before the build starts where something is expensive to do in Framer.

items.question: Can you build our online store in Framer?
items.answer: No. Selling belongs on Shopify, and that is a separate service — see /shopify-development, where we do storefront conversion work and migrations onto Shopify. We will happily build the marketing site around a store and link the two.

items.question: What about our product's app interface?
items.answer: That is product design, not a marketing site, and it is a different service — see /ui-ux-design. There we design SaaS and web app interfaces in Figma and hand off specs your developers build from. Framer is where the site that sells the product lives; it is not where the product lives.

items.question: How long does a site take?
items.answer: A campaign landing page is days. A full marketing site is usually four to eight weeks, and the variable is almost never the build — it is how long the content takes to land. We agree the page map and the content owner in the first step precisely because that is what moves the date.
